status_summary: USAID no longer exists, so the outcome is judged in State, Treasury and the wider executive branch, where the cessation elements of the text are operative but the affirmative support for oil and gas in aid programs was not found. Executive Order 14162 (signed 2025-01-20) revoked the US International Climate Finance Plan, ended UNFCCC financial commitments and directed that foreign energy engagement prioritize economic efficiency and American prosperity, and a memorandum of 2026-01-07 directed withdrawal from bodies including the UNFCCC, the IPCC and the International Renewable Energy Agency, ceasing funding to the extent permitted by law. The Treasury Secretary urged the World Bank in April 2025 to adopt an all-of-the-above energy approach that includes gas rather than climate finance targets, and the EXIM board, an export credit agency rather than an aid agency, approved a loan of nearly $5 billion for the Mozambique LNG project on 2025-03-14. The FY2026 law still funds the Global Environment Facility at $150.2 million, and the rescission of the 2021 interim guidance on overseas fossil fuel financing was not verified, so the record is held at the bottom of the implemented band.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14162 was signed (published 2025-01-30 at 90 FR 8455); Sec. 3(e) revoked the US International Climate Finance Plan, Sec. 3(c) directed ceasing UNFCCC financial commitments, Sec. 3(f) required agency reports on rescinding policies that advanced the plan, and Sec. 3(g) set priorities of economic efficiency and American prosperity for foreign energy engagement.
The US EXIM board approved a loan of nearly $5 billion for the TotalEnergies-led Mozambique LNG project, clearing a hurdle to restart it.
The Treasury Secretary urged the World Bank to expand energy access with technologies that sustain growth rather than meet climate finance targets, and said climate work is outside the IMF's mission.

The US statement to the IMF's policy committee (meeting of 2025-04-24 to 2025-04-25) called for an all-of-the-above approach to energy at the World Bank that includes gas and welcomed the plan to lift its nuclear ban.

The World Bank board decided to end its ban on financing nuclear energy projects, a change the US had pushed for, without agreeing on upstream gas financing (dated by the report; the decision date is not stated in the source).

A presidential memorandum was signed (published 2026-01-16 at 91 FR 2281) directing withdrawal from 66 international organizations (35 non-UN and 31 UN entities), including the UNFCCC, the IPCC and the International Renewable Energy Agency, with participation in or funding to UN entities to cease to the extent permitted by law.

The House Appropriations Committee's undated summary of the final FY2026 bill (enacted as P.L. 119-75) says it eliminates funding for the prior administration's climate executive orders and climate change mandates.
CRS reported FY2026 enacted funding for the Global Environment Facility of $150.2 million.

title: Stop opposing fossil fuel development abroad and narrow climate funding in foreign aid
uncertainties: The rescission of the 2021 interim guidance on international public financing of fossil fuel projects and of Treasury's multilateral development bank energy guidance was not confirmed: the researcher's searches and one reviewer search returned only 2021 coverage of the guidance. EO 14162 does not name those documents. The IMFC statement prints only April 2025; the date 2025-04-25 is taken from the meeting dates on the statement. The House committee summary prints no date and is dated here to the law's enactment; it gives no figures for the climate eliminations, and CRS lists zero FY2026 funding for the Clean Technology Fund and for Tropical Forest and Coral Reef Conservation without explanation. A search for DFC financing of oil or gas projects in 2025 or 2026 returned only older financings. EXIM is an export credit agency, so its LNG loan is a parallel step, not foreign aid. Whether specific climate-advocacy NGOs and foundations lost funding was not separately verified; the withdrawal memorandum covers international bodies only. Mandate text on the Climate Strategy 2022 to 2030 and Paris-related programs is tracked in c09-03. Division F of P.L. 119-75 could not be read: the GovInfo HTML ends within Division A, Title VIII (Sec. 8072) and does not reach Division F, so the Global Environment Facility line was confirmed only through the CRS report and any climate-order funding limit only through the House committee summary. EO 14162 was read in full on the Federal Register and contains no provision on fossil fuel financing guidance or on funding climate-advocacy organizations.
